statement: A documented, multi-item release checklist step executed correctly by hand across several prior releases can still be skipped on a later one -- being written down and followed before does not prevent recurrence. Incident: cejel commit a6bf7d7 ('release: 0.4.8') bumped package.json/server.json/published-versions.json to 0.4.8 but left six README distribution-pin mentions (Windows signing note, npm distribution note, two Docker/OCI run examples, OpenClaw MCP example) at 0.4.7, though docs/release-process.md documents the step and every prior cut (0.4.4-0.4.7, e.g. commit 8354ffd) bumped all six together. CI's validate:distribution caught the mismatch and blocked PR #295's merge until fixed in commit 0a421ae. Rule: what actually prevents a checklist item from being dropped is a mechanical check that re-derives every occurrence from one intended-version source of truth and fails loud on mismatch -- not the checklist's track record.

anchors.summary: Fixed the release/0.4.8 -> main PR after CI's validate:distribution blocked it: bumped the six README distribution-pin mentions from 0.4.7 to 0.4.8 that release commit a6bf7d7 had skipped, matching the pattern every prior release cut followed in its own version-bump commit.
